identity: A near-static, low, wide, rear-side poster shot of the acting character (left) facing the enemy (right), which hosts the whole menu as a fan of labels pinned to the character, and which every command interrupts with a hard-cut, comic-timed cutaway or a flat 2D graphic set piece, so each turn plays like edited anime and manga panels rather than a tracking camera.
method: Text claims come from opened pages (Sources). Camera claims are marked [observed: video m:ss] when I saw the moment in a decoded frame of an official upload (headless Chromium; 1280x720 for most, 640x360 for the Take Over trailer and 854x480 for Change The World; frames deleted afterwards); base-game phases that no official upload shows were observed in two unofficial captures, which are listed as sources but never offered as watch links. Camera height, lens and angle are eyeballed from frames: no source publishes Persona 5 battle-camera parameters.
corrections: The character eyes-strip cut-in is the weakness cut-in that plays when the chosen skill hits a known weakness (PlayStation.Blog Japan/Dengeki; observed on a weakness Persona cast at ATLUS Japan early-story video 3:58.2-3:58.6 and absent on a non-weakness Persona skill at 4:12-4:13.6). It is not the 1 MORE title. 1 MORE is a large white typographic title that follows the knockdown (observed in an unofficial capture at 10:06, no official frame found).
The Japanese build says Baton Touch (バトンタッチ) where the English build says Baton Pass.
cameraGrammar: Two camera modes only: a stable hero shot that holds indefinitely while the player thinks, and short authored cutaways (about 0.3 to 5 s) on every commit. [derived from observed frames]

While a menu is open the camera does not move; the UI animates (ring fans out from the character's hand, list slides, reticle hops). Background shift over 4 to 19 s of command select measured 0 px. [observed: ATLUS Japan early-story video 3:52-3:56; unofficial capture 1:40-1:59]
Every cut lands under a graphic beat: ink wipe, shard wipe, typographic burst (WEAK, 1 MORE, HOLD UP!, BATON PASS!), comic panel. The graphic hides the cut and adds the sound-effect feel. [derived]

The camera is always on the action's owner or its victim, never on a neutral master; the party HP cards stay pinned bottom-right through 3D cutaways and disappear only in the 2D sequences and Showtime. [observed]
The climaxes leave the 3D scene: All-Out Attack becomes a flat red plane of silhouettes, Showtime becomes a purpose-built cutscene stage. [observed]

Persona 5's director describes the intended feel as turn-based battle built like a cutscene, using the cut-and-paste method of anime and manga; the Clair Obscur creative director describes the same effect as the camera shifting dramatically with each action, like watching a movie. [Persona Central 2023; PCGamesN 2025]

shots.name: Ambush strike, ink wipe, shard reveal

camera.where: Field: third-person behind Joker. On the strike the camera jams in behind his shoulder against the target, cuts to a dark starfield cut-in of Joker mid-leap, then to extreme close-ups of the target. The battle intro is a red-glow shot from just behind Joker's hip looking up at the enemy; a white crack and a black-and-white shard wipe reveal the normal command shot.
camera.height: Waist to chest in the field and wipe; ground-skimming in the leap cut-in.
camera.distance: Close: the target or Joker coat fills most of the frame until the reveal.
camera.movement: Hard cuts hidden behind ink shapes and one whip-pan; no dolly, no crane, no fly-in over the arena.

shots.frame: Ink-black and red shapes, the enemy silhouette, neon casino signs tumbling past as a montage element. Party HUD hidden (only a small hint bottom-right). In the English build the AMBUSH! title bursts over the impact with a red ink splash.
shots.timing: About 9 s from strike to command shot in the ATLUS clip (3:40 to 3:49): close-ups 3:40-3:42, ink wipe 3:42-3:45, red-glow intro 3:45-3:48, shard wipe 3:48. In an English capture the title holds about 1 s (1:03-1:04) and the fight is at the command shot by 1:06.
shots.whyItWorks: The transition is graphic design rather than camera motion: ink shapes cover the cut, so the arrival at the stable shot feels earned and the player never watches a load or a fly-in.

shots.name: Rear-side poster shot with the menu ring pinned to the character

camera.where: Behind and to the left of the acting character, who stands in the left third in three-quarter rear view; the enemy stands right of centre facing back. About 50 degrees off the line from party to enemy.
camera.height: Hip to waist height, tilted slightly up at the enemy.
camera.distance: Mid-close: the character is about half the frame height and the enemy is taller.
camera.movement: None. Background shift between frames 4 s apart (232 s and 236 s) and 19 s apart (unofficial capture) measured 0 px by phase correlation; only idle animation and UI motion move.

shots.frame: Character in the left third. A fan of angled black label plates with red slashes (GUN, PERSONA, ITEM, SWORD, GUARD, plus ORDER when the party has more than one member) is anchored at the character's hand and hip and points at the enemy. Red target marker with a heart icon on the enemy. Enemy name-and-level plate top-left; navigator speech bubble with portrait top-right; one to four slanted HP/SP cards bottom-right (a solo fight shows one); five button hints bottom-left (Analyze, Target, turn-order or status check, Rush, Assist) in the same order with the same icons in the base and Royal frames (the wording of the third hint differs between the English base capture and the Japanese Royal frames; localisation or Royal change not established).
shots.timing: Holds until input. No auto-orbit and no idle drift.
shots.whyItWorks: The composition doubles as the menu: hero left, enemy right, UI in the space between, so the screen reads as a poster and the eye travels from hero to enemy. Because the shot is static, the ring, not the camera, does all the animating.
shots.confidence: [verified: 3 sources] observed base (ATLUS Japan early-story 3:52-3:56), observed Royal (ATLUS Japan Vol.3 1:16 and Vol.2 1:07), and a design write-up that puts the character left and the monster right with every button pointing at the acting character [single source: Wen blog]. camera.where: Not a camera move but a stack of graphics on the wide shot: (1) when the chosen skill hits a known weakness, a horizontal jagged strip of the caster's eyes plays first; (2) the hit; (3) a WEAK or CRITICAL burst with the damage number and a cyan heart over the target; (4) the target drops and the frame may desaturate for a beat; (5) a large white 1 MORE title; (6) the command ring returns with a BATON PASS tag.
camera.movement: Hard cuts; the eyes strip lasts about 0.5 s.

shots.frame: The eyes strip spans the middle third of the screen over blue Persona aura; the WEAK burst is red and white above the enemy; the 1 MORE title is about a fifth of the frame; the navigator comments top-right.
shots.timing: Eyes strip 3:58.2-3:58.6 (0.4 to 0.5 s); WEAK burst about 1 s; 1 MORE about 0.5 s; cast to next command about 8 to 10 s.
shots.whyItWorks: The reward is stated three ways in under two seconds (face, word, title) and the extra turn is signalled by the returning ring, so the player never wonders whether the weakness worked.
shots.confidence: [verified: 2 sources] for the weakness cut-in: PlayStation.Blog Japan/Dengeki says a weakness skill triggers a character cut-in; strip observed on the first Persona cast (ATLUS Japan early-story 3:58.2-3:58.6) and absent on a second Persona skill later in the same fight (4:12-4:13.6); whether that second skill hit a weakness is not established, so the rule rests on the Dengeki text. royalChanges.detail: Chance-triggered pair attacks staged as bespoke cutscenes in their own sets with HUD off; a large prompt appears (touchpad on PS4), the offer expires if unused, they can be skipped, and they vary slightly against bosses. Panther and Fox: about 16 s.

royalChanges.detail: Rank raises attack and recovery, restores HP or SP at the pass, and a fourth pass makes the last member's skill cost zero; the choice view shows a rank card. Passing is available from the start. Pass staging and camera are otherwise the same as the base game in the frames seen.
royalChanges.source: PlayStation.Blog Japan; Push Square; TheGamer; ATLUS Japan Vol.3 1:21-1:40 (observed)

royalChanges.detail: Futaba can randomly deliver the finishing card in Royal. Staging of the silhouette brawl and the finish card is otherwise the same as the base game.

devStatements.who: Katsura Hashino, director (Denfaminicogamer interview 2023-04-25, translated by Persona Central)
devStatements.summary: Turn-based battles stay viable if they fit as part of a cutscene's composition: show the scenes that need showing, and use the cut-and-paste method of anime and manga scenes; the Persona 5 team chose turn-based on that basis and kept attack and Persona summon to a single button press for tempo.

The earliest UI was aggressively animated to the point that it was hard to see what was going on; messages were too diagonal, so the animations were calmed and rotations reduced to balance style and usability.

devStatements.who: Katsura Hashino (4Gamer interview, 2016, translated by Persona Central)
devStatements.summary: Hold Up came from films where a villain holds people at gunpoint; the thieves move in a way that shows they know how cool they look.

devStatements.who: Atlus UI team (Kazuhisa Wada and Masaki Sudou/Suto, CEDEC+KYUSHU 2017, reported by Siliconera and Famitsu)
devStatements.summary: Persona 5's UI uses red as its one key colour (no sub-colours except on the HP/SP elements), central lines to guide the eye, and a tool that renders a 3D model spinning into a pose as 2D art; separate designers handled the menu and the battle-scene UI, and the battle designer checked every frame with the programmer. The Famitsu report does not discuss the battle camera.

devStatements.who: Guillaume Broche, Sandfall Interactive (Denfaminicogamer interview, May 2025; reported by PCGamesN and Automaton West)
devStatements.summary: Calls Persona 5 the best game in the world for UI and combat visuals; the camera shifting dramatically with each player action, like watching a movie, left a huge impression. He wanted to bring that quality of camera work and presentation into Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, and says there is more he wants to take from Persona 5, especially in the UI. This is the one source found that ties a later game's battle camera to Persona 5.

devStatements.who: Koji Ise, Atlus lead interface designer (GDC 2025; reported by Noisy Pixel and PC Gamer)
devStatements.summary: For Metaphor: ReFantazio the team explicitly worked to differentiate its visual identity from Persona; the battle screen uses a bird's-eye view because in the story the king watches from above. He also said a stripped-down UI option is something Atlus is considering. No source found says Metaphor's battle camera derives from Persona 5.

devStatements.who: Katsura Hashino on Metaphor: ReFantazio (Official Xbox Podcast, October 2024; reported by GamesRadar)
devStatements.summary: Metaphor mixes real-time and command battles to bring in the idea of manga and movie-style combat, and the fast and slow tempo balance was refined from the team's previous games.
